{"notes": "Visit 5, left at 7:45. Nobody spoke while I was there. The picture is unchanged from visit 4: one unbroken dark chain from start along the back, round the nose at x=3, down the belly to the tail tip near x=28, y=15. No pale dominoes, no gaps, doubled patches (back x=11-14, belly x=17-19) still connected. No hand labels visible, so nobody was touching the fish. The team seems to have stayed hands-off before the push, which is good discipline. I still can't attribute any domino to a person, so the result can't be credited individually.

Hana: Silent this visit. Owned the tail tip, which is finished and connected, consistent with her plan, though I never saw her place it. Leadership is still the strongest evidence: clear roles and handoffs that others followed. Execution is partly self-reported.

Jack: Silent this visit. Last visit he said 'Nice one, Omar. Hands off from me, all set for the push.' That showed recognition of a teammate and stepping back properly. His concrete contribution is still unknown. He said he'd watch for gaps and none appeared.

Sofia: Silent this visit. Her 6:15 report 'All set here. Hands off' matched the picture and her earlier belly report. She is reliable, collaborative, and stayed in her lane. What she placed is still unconfirmed.

Omar: Silent this visit. Jack credited him last visit, which is vague peer evidence. Earlier he verified the middle section accurately. What he built is still unknown.

No ratings yet. Before the review, ask each person privately what they placed, and ask what Jack's praise of Omar referred to. Without that, impact and execution rest on self-reports and peer remarks. The fish is complete and the push is still to come."}
